_meta.indication: MULTAQ is indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular hospitalization in patients with paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) or atrial flutter (AFL), with a recent episode of AF/AFL and associated cardiovascular risk factors (age >70, hypertension, diabetes, prior cerebrovascular accident, left atrial diameter ≥50 mm or LVEF <40%), who are in sinus rhythm or who will be cardioverted.

pivotal_trials.phase: Clinical phase not stated in the reviewed documents.
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of MULTAQ 400 mg twice daily (2301 patients) vs placebo (2327 patients), treated for up to 30 months (median follow-up 22 months).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with a recent history of AF/AFL who were in sinus rhythm or to be converted to sinus rhythm; ≥75 years old, or ≥70 years old with at least one risk factor (hypertension, diabetes, prior cerebrovascular accident, left atrial diameter ≥50 mm or LVEF <0.40).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: time to first hospitalization for cardiovascular reasons or death from any cause.
pivotal_trials.result: MULTAQ reduced the combined endpoint of cardiovascular hospitalization or death from any cause by 24.2% vs placebo: 727 (31.6%) vs 913 (39.2%), HR 0.76 [0.68-0.83], p<0.0001; all-cause death was not significantly different (115 [5.0%] vs 135 [5.8%], HR 0.86 [0.67-1.11], p=0.24).

nct_ctgov.title: A Trial With Dronedarone to Prevent Hospitalization or Death in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation

key_safety: Most frequent adverse reactions were diarrhea (9% vs 6% placebo), nausea (5% vs 3%), abdominal pain (4% vs 3%), vomiting (2% vs 1%), and asthenic conditions (7% vs 5%); serum creatinine increased ≥10% in 51% vs 21% placebo. Premature discontinuation due to adverse reactions occurred in 11.8% of dronedarone-treated vs 7.7% of placebo. Most serious risk: increased mortality in severe heart failure patients (boxed warning).
target_moa: Antiarrhythmic drug; a structural analog of amiodarone with antiarrhythmic properties belonging to all four Vaughan-Williams classes (beta-adrenergic, sodium channel, and IKr potassium channel effects), though the precise mechanism and contribution of each activity to the clinical effect is unknown.
modality: Small molecule (dronedarone hydrochloride, an amiodarone analog lacking iodine substituents).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: HEART FAILURE — MULTAQ is contraindicated in patients with NYHA Class IV heart failure, or NYHA Class II-III heart failure with a recent decompensation requiring hospitalization or referral to a specialized heart failure clinic. In the ANDROMEDA Study, patients given dronedarone had a greater than two-fold increase in mortality.

rems.type: A REMS was required and approved, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: The Advisory Committee favored (10 to 3) approval of dronedarone, and recommended excluding patients with advanced (NYHA Class III or IV) heart failure or those recently hospitalized with heart failure.

summary.text: MULTAQ (dronedarone) NDA 22-425 received priority review because the new indication included a mortality benefit, was supported by the ATHENA outcomes trial, reviewed with a 10-to-3 favorable advisory committee vote, and approved effective on the date of the approval letter (signed July 1, 2009) with a required REMS (Medication Guide and communication plan) and multiple postmarketing required epidemiologic/pharmacovigilance studies. It was a standard (full) approval, not an accelerated approval.
